button.description: No type. Defaults to submit when inside a form.
button.statusNote: Without a type, buttons default to type="submit".

button-submit.statusNote: Use inside a form for the primary action.

button-reset.statusNote: Rare. Confusing for users; consider omitting.

input-submit.description: Submits the parent form. Label comes from value.

input-button.statusNote: Avoid. Prefer a button element with type="button".

input-reset.description: Resets the parent form. Label comes from value.
input-reset.statusNote: Rare. Confusing for users; consider omitting.

input-image.description: An image used as a submit button. The image is the visible label and the alt attribute provides the accessible name.
input-image.statusNote: Submits the form and includes click coordinates in the payload.

input-checkbox-switch.description: A native checkbox with role="switch". The browser handles label-click forwarding, keyboard activation, and focus for free when linked to a sibling label element.
input-checkbox-switch.statusNote: Easiest accessible switch when the value is submitted as form data.

text.statusNote: The default input type. Use for general short text entry like a name or subject line.

email.statusNote: Triggers the email keyboard on mobile devices. Pair with autocomplete="email" for autofill.

tel.statusNote: Triggers the phone keyboard on mobile devices. Does not validate format — use the pattern attribute or JavaScript for that.

url.statusNote: Triggers a URL keyboard with a .com key on mobile devices.

password.statusNote: Masks the input visually. Browsers offer password manager integration; do not disable it.

number.statusNote: Restricts input to digits and strips leading zeros — avoid for credit card numbers, phone numbers, and postal codes; use inputmode="numeric" on a text input instead.

search.statusNote: Triggers the search keyboard on mobile devices and may add a clear button to the input.

input-checkbox.statusNote: The native checkbox. Browsers handle keyboard activation, label-click forwarding, and accessible role for free.

div-checkbox.statusNote: A styled div with role="checkbox". You must add aria-checked yourself to expose the state.

input-radio.statusNote: The native radio. Browsers handle arrow-key navigation, mutual exclusion within a shared name, and accessible role for free.

select-native.description: The native single-choice select element. Renders as the platform picker — a wheel on iOS, a list on Android, an OS dropdown on desktop.
select-native.statusNote: Browsers handle keyboard activation, type-ahead, focus management, and accessible role for free.

select-multiple.description: Native multi-select with the multiple attribute. Renders as a visible list-box; users hold Cmd/Ctrl to select more than one.
select-multiple.statusNote: The multi-select interaction is not visually discoverable — pair it with a usage hint near the field.

div-combobox.description: A div with role="combobox" — no listbox, no aria-controls, no keyboard handling. The canonical broken-custom-select pattern.
div-combobox.statusNote: Avoid. Sighted mouse users see a dropdown; keyboard and screen reader users cannot operate the control.
